minutes.headline: Parks Commission voted to raise Town Beach and swim-lesson fees for 2026 to cut the town's subsidy.
minutes.summary: The Parks Commission set new 2026 Town Beach season/day pass rates and swim lesson fees, explicitly aiming to move the beach program toward being self-sustaining ahead of a possible town override vote. It also amended and adopted a park facilities signage policy, corrected a prior vote on the Fitzgerald Field sign, and gave updates on the recreation director search, the skate park entry-agreement negotiation, a private team's field rental, and a proposed vendor-fair partnership with Lunenburg Youth Baseball/the select board.

votes.motion: Move ahead with a new Fitzgerald Field sign funded from the Parks revolving account (correcting the agenda item from the prior meeting)
Set 2026 Town Beach resident and non-resident season and day pass rates as just read
Set 2026 swim lesson rates: resident $50 per child per session capped at $150 per family; non-resident $60 per child per session capped at $180 per family
Approve the park facilities signage policy as amended tonight

budget_items.what_was_said: Commission corrected a prior vote to allow the facilities director to move ahead with a new sign at Fitzgerald Field, funded from the Parks revolving account.
The beach salary line was appropriated for the current fiscal year but has already been overspent, before the summer season even begins.
Total salary cost for the 2025 beach season, spanning the June-to-August season across two fiscal years, was given.
The contracted landscaping company's costs for weeding, cleanups, sand maintenance, deep cleanings, supplies/repairs and utilities were listed as ranges.
Revenue collected through swim lessons, season passes and day passes at the beach for 2025 was totaled.
Commission read back the full new rate schedule for resident and non-resident family, individual, senior and day passes before voting on it.
New per-child, per-session swim lesson rates with a family cap were set for residents and non-residents.
Staff estimated how much additional revenue the new pass rates would bring in if sales volume stayed the same as last year, compared to last year's total.
Even with the new rates, projected beach revenue was said to still fall short of covering the beach's costs.
If beach revenue does not cover costs, the commission noted the revolving account could cover the difference, estimating that cost.
A private out-of-town youth baseball program requesting weekend use of McNally Field would be charged the town's existing per-player field-use rate.

transfers.description: Parks revolving account covering any shortfall between Town Beach revenue and costs

decisions.decision: Decided not to participate in this year's Earth Day event given no recreation director is in place; will reconsider once one is hired.

Facilities director will review the skate park's third-party peer-review documents with the town manager first, then bring questions to the commission before a joint meeting with the skate park group.
Aim to have a skate park entry/license agreement executed before the chair and another departing commissioner leave in May.
Held off finalizing the field usage forms and policy so an incoming recreation director can be part of that conversation.
Removed the Park Commission itself from sign-approval authority in the draft signage policy, leaving approval to the facilities director or recreation director instead.

Chair will put in writing to Lunenburg Youth Baseball/Josie that the town cannot commit staff support for the vendor fair until a recreation director is hired, and will invite her to the next meeting to discuss a partnership.
Kept the regular meeting schedule on the fourth Wednesday, setting the next meeting for March 25.

what_happened.line: The Parks Commission voted to raise 2026 Town Beach season and day pass rates, aiming to shrink the town's subsidy of the beach program.
The Commission also voted, 3-0, to raise 2026 swim lesson rates, with a per-family cap for both residents and non-residents.
Staff said the new rates are still projected to fall short of covering the beach's costs, with the Parks revolving account as a possible backstop for the gap.
The Commission adopted an amended park facilities signage policy that removes the Commission itself from sign-approval authority, shifting it to staff.
Field-use rules and a proposed vendor-fair partnership were held off until a recreation director is hired, a position still vacant.

why_it_matters: This sets what residents and non-residents pay for beach passes and swim lessons in 2026, and it comes up in the context of a possible town override vote on covering town costs.
The rate increase is presented as narrowing, not closing, the gap between beach revenue and beach costs, so the shortfall may still draw on other town funds.
Sign approval at town park facilities now rests with staff rather than the elected Commission, changing who signs off on that kind of decision going forward.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The four formal votes (Fitzgerald sign, beach passes, swim lessons, signage policy) agree on outcome and count in both records, and most decisions line up in substance. The two diverge on: several dollar figures the official minutes never mention (projected revenue increase, the revenue-vs-cost shortfall, the revolving-account backstop amount), a swapped organization name (our minutes say "Lunenburg Youth Baseball/Josie" where the official minutes say "Lunenburg Business Association"), a dropped condition on the signage vote ("pending approval from the Building Commissioner"), and the Chair's name (Karen Bernard vs. Karin Menard) — a reader relying on either record alone would miss real content the other one has.
